candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XX.1 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage' — Ephrem reads the Pascal preface as the ground of every command that follows. The commandments are not arbitrary statutes but the rule-of-life of a delivered people; only the delivered are addressed by the Decalogue. Tewahedo catechesis preserves this priority of deliverance before commandment.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XX.4 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy' — Ephrem reads Sabbath-rest as the canonical sign that creation is given a goal beyond labour: the Sabbath foreshadows the eighth-day rest of the Resurrection. Tewahedo alone among the major communions preserves both observances together — Saturday-Sabbath retained from Sinai and Sunday-Lord's-Day added from the Resurrection — and reads Ex 20:8 as the canonical anchor of the double observance.
